current.text: He signed with the New Orleans Pelicans and joins them as a bench player.
He is not in the projected Pelicans starting lineup. Dejounte Murray, Trey Murphy and Zion Williamson are locked in, Yves Missi likely starts, and the last spot goes to Jeremiah Fears or Herb Jones.
He is projected for about eight fewer minutes per game than last season. He would compete for shots with Fears, Murphy, Murray and Zion.
The Pelicans have more players than they have minutes for, so roles on the team are hard to project.
The Pelicans may need to trade someone to make room for him, possibly Jordan Hawkins or Micah Peavy.
The Pelicans have a new head coach, Jamahl Mosley.
Experts see the Pelicans as a weak team near the bottom of the West, at about 34 wins.

durable.text: He drives well and gets to the rim and the free throw line. FT% is his best category.
He does not defend, pass or shoot well, and his defensive and shooting numbers are bad.
He has improved as a rebounder.

note: Both sites price him at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 160, ESPN rank 189). That puts him outside our 144-player draft, though our league paid 4 USD for him last season. Yahoo projects only 11.2 points on 8.2 shots as a bench player, while ESPN still projects 16.5 points in 29 minutes. Do not draft him. Watch him on waivers early. If New Orleans clears its crowded rotation with a trade, or Zion or a starting guard misses time, his FT% (86.9% on 6.2 attempts last season) and his points could return.
